title: Queued credit leak during orchestrator failover triggering sustained tenant degradation
creator: Tessa Moreno
description: Summary: Several customers on Dedicated and Private observed sustained elevated 429s after a regional orchestrator failover. Root cause appears to be a queuing/commit race in the local rate-limiter ledger where queued credit tokens for burst windows are marked as allocated but not reconciled back to tenant state after leader handoff, leading to long-lived credit starvation. Impact: affected tenants saw degraded throughput for 15-90 minutes post-failover, with lower-tier routes hit hardest. Multiple escalations opened by Enterprise accounts; some required manual tenant credit resets. Reproduction notes: simulated failover in staging with synthetic burst traffic and delayed ledger flush reproduces the stuck-queued entries. We observed orphaned queue entries on the standby orchestrator that never applied expiration reconciliation because the epoch reconciliation job mis-identified their origin during transient leadership change. Immediate mitigation: rolled out a hotfix on orchestrator that forces a reconciliation sweep during leadership acquisition (hotfix runtime-1.25-hotpatch-2026-03-11) and exposed an emergency admin endpoint for manual queued-credit scavenging. Long-term fix proposals: 1) change commit protocol so queued credits are persisted with a stable owner ID and reconciliation TTL that survives failover; 2) add idempotent reconciliation pass on leader election to re-evaluate queued tokens and re-apply or release them atomically; 3) add metric and alert for queued-credit-age and reconciliation-latency; 4) add a canary for leader-swap reconciliation in staging that validates no tenant credit leakage for 10k requests. Rollout plan: implement protocol change behind runtime feature flag, test on staging and a single dedicated region; then progressive rollout to hosted, dedicated, and private with telemetry verification. Backfill tasks: update runbooks, create an operator script for safe scavenging, and include this scenario in disaster recovery tests. Links: Slack incident channel: slack.redwood#inc-queued-credit-leak, Confluence PRA: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Queued+Credit+Leak+PRA, Monitoring dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ql/queued-credit?orgId=1, Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/8291

2026-03-11 - 08:12 UTC - SRE (Maya Singh): Hotfix PR created and merged: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/8291. Patch forces reconciliation on leader election and instruments queued-credit-age metric.

2026-03-12 - 16:30 UTC - Ravi Patel: Postmortem draft started. Initial hypothesis: ledger write-path race + missing owner metadata on queued credits when we fast-path in-memory queueing during failover.

2026-03-13 - 11:42 UTC - QA (Evan Brooks): Added automated staging test that simulates leader transitions under 50 concurrent burst clients; failing cases reproduced consistently before hotpatch and pass with patched reconciler.
2026-03-13 - 15:00 UTC - Ravi Patel: Filed follow-ups: ENG-141210 (protocol-owner-id), ENG-141211 (reconciliation-idempotency), ENG-141212 (dashboard-alerts). Scheduling for next sprint.
